expected_title: Nanosat Orbit Raising and Rendezvous Using a Continuous-Thrust Controller
abstract: This study presents a propulsive controller for a combined orbit change and formation flying for two nanosats (leader-follower) assuming continuously firing thrusters with input constraints. The nanosats are assumed to be released at a nominal International Space Station (ISS) orbit and a transfer orbit is implemented so they reach the desired orbit. Then a rendezvous maneuver is implemented using a “virtual” nanosat that maintains a desired distance between the two nanosats. The control design for the first stage of the mission is based on Gauss’ variational equations, suitable for continuous-thrust trajectory control. The rendezvous design for the second stage, is based on the nonlinear equations of relative motion between the follower nanosat and the virtual nanosat, and uses an adaptive backstepping control method. To demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed control algorithm, two case studies are considered. The first case study considers an orbit raising maneuver with a subsequent formation flying maneuver that keeps the two nanosats separated to an arc distance of 100 km. The second case study considers an orbit lowering maneuver with a subsequent formation flying maneuver that also maintains the two nanosats to an arc distance of 100 km.
